runs.text: The Luri live primarily in the western and southwestern regions of Iran, particularly in and around the Zagros mountains. Some Luri live in Iraq. They are nomadic peoples who work as
shepherds

and travel six to eight months of the year, living in black, goat-hair tents. They live in permanent dwellings for a few months during the winter. Some Luri have settled in villages preferring farming to shepherding. Wheat and barley are their principal crops.

The Luri believe that a shepherd’s success is determined by his personal qualities and good luck. Luri society is dominated by those possessing the largest flocks and the most money. This upper class hires members of the lower class to tend to their flocks. Most of the Luri belong to the lower class of society.

The Luri are practicing Shia Muslims. They have adopted a very practical belief system with simple religious practices. They love shrines dedicated to holy men (founders of various Islamic groups) and use them as pilgrimage sites. Because these shrines are believed to possess healing powers, people with physical and psychological ailments visit them each year in hope of being cured.
There are only a few known Luri Christians. There is some evangelistic material available in their language.

The Luri are divided into political units called tribes, or “il.” Each tribe is headed by a hereditary chief, or khan, who is recruited by one of the sub-tribes. Pray that they will hear of the one true chief, the King of Kings.
“I am the good
shepherd
. The good
shepherd
lays down his life for the sheep.”
John 10:11
Pray that the Luri, whether nomadic shepherds or settled farmers, will one day hear the voice of Jesus,
the Good Shepherd
, and recognize that they are also among the “other sheep” He longs to bring into His flock.
Pray that tribal chiefs will come to faith in Christ and share the good news with the rest of their tribe.
Pray that the message of Christ will break through the strong class divisions within Luri society, bringing unity, dignity, and hope as they discover the one flock under one Shepherd.

Pray that the few Luri believers will be strengthened in their faith and find others to fellowship with regularly. Pray that the Iranian church will have a desire to reach out to the Luri people and find ways to connect with them and share the Good news.
Pray that workers will be raised up that will live among the Luri and love them unconditionally.
